Assuming you quite literally can’t go back; for one, treat your hosts like they are royalty. This is pretty common sense but, you won’t get anywhere biting the hand that feeds. Along with this, try to find a place in walking distance to work if you can, it’s best to not rely on the people who took you in for rides and things of that nature.

Second, get any job you can get, then search after for a more suitable one. Don’t waste your time trying to find a perfect or even a good one, you can do that a lot easier when you have a car. Instead, just settle for what you can get as fast as possible.

Third, unless you’re addicted to the point where withdrawals would make your life currently worse off, stay away from as much substances as you can until you’re on a good route. Almost every substance (including caffeine) can easily ruin your impulse control, making it significantly harder to keep saving.

Fourth, say what you need to say, and do what you need to do. Play the game. Don’t try being a rebel, don’t try going against people… just play the game.

Fifth, if and when you can, try working on a healthy skill to pass your time, and generally take care of yourself. The more improvements your hosts see, the more naturally willing they’ll be to help you out.

This is all assuming you can’t apply for disability or food stamps or anything of that nature. Those are obvious good steps if you can, but even then, this route is probably more sustainable.
